title: 448 - Harlem Globetrotters
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Harlem Globetrotters
items.description: The episode's game: GameTek's 1991 NES basketball game, an exhibition match with only a few trick shots.

links.label: Harlem Globetrotters - The Cutting Room Floor
Harlem Globetrotters (NES) - Video Game Music Preservation Foundation

items.name: Harlem Globetrotters (the team)
items.description: The exhibition basketball team the game is licensed from, and the subject of Mike's childhood game story.

items.name: Washington Generals
items.description: The Globetrotters' perpetual opponents, who famously won once, and who you can pick in the game.

items.name: GameTek
items.description: The publisher of the game, whose manual has six pages of ads for its other games and which later went bankrupt.

items.name: National Basketball Association
items.description: The league the hosts say has ignored the Globetrotters' winning streak.

items.name: Space Jam
items.description: Mike's joke that Michael Jordan was promised he'd play for the Generals if the Looney Tunes lost.

items.name: Michael Jordan
items.description: The star of Space Jam, in the hosts' joke about playing for the Washington Generals.

items.name: Savannah Bananas
items.description: The baseball novelty act the hosts say is doing for baseball what the Globetrotters did for basketball.

items.name: Double Dribble
items.description: The earlier NES basketball game with cut-in dunk scenes, which the hosts say feels more like a Globetrotters game.

items.name: The Simpsons: Bart vs. the Space Mutants
items.description: Last week's game, whose theme song worry Mike compares to the Globetrotters' theme being included.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Simpsons: Bart vs. the Space Mutants

items.episode_title: The Simpsons: Bart vs The Space Mutants

items.name: Sweet Georgia Brown
items.description: The whistled theme tune the Globetrotters play, which the hosts try and fail to whistle.

links.label: Wikipedia: Sweet Georgia Brown
links.note: 1925 song by Ben Bernie, Maceo Pinkard, and Kenneth Casey

items.name: Harlem Shake
items.description: The other track Mike jokes the game includes.

items.name: Meet the Mets
items.description: The New York Mets' team song, offered as a rare sports-team theme.

items.name: Roman Reigns
items.description: One of the wrestlers with an entrance theme, in the hosts' comparison to the Globetrotters' theme song.

items.name: Dwayne Johnson
items.description: Another wrestler-turned-actor with an entrance theme, "The Rock".

items.name: Kayfabe
items.description: The wrestling term for keeping a staged event believable, used to describe the Globetrotters.

links.label: Wikipedia: Kayfabe
links.note: Portrayal of professional wrestling events as being real

items.name: Interstellar
items.description: The film Sean brings up in the Yankees-as-a-novelty-act riff.

items.name: New York Yankees
items.description: Used in the hosts' joke about MLB disappearing and the Yankees becoming a traveling novelty act.

items.name: Wheel of Fortune
items.description: One of GameTek's game-show games advertised in the manual.

items.name: Jeopardy
items.description: Another of GameTek's NES game-show games.

items.name: Classic Concentration
items.description: GameTek's NES version of the Concentration game show.

items.name: Double Dare
items.description: The Nickelodeon-based game GameTek also published.

items.name: Hollywood Squares
items.description: Another GameTek game-show adaptation advertised in the manual.

items.name: Super Password
items.description: The word-association game show behind the unreleased NES game.

links.label: Wikipedia: Password Plus and Super Password

items.name: Talking Super Password
items.description: The cancelled NES game advertised in the manual with box art, of which no prototype is known to have surfaced.

links.label: Super Password (lost builds of unreleased NES port) - The Lost Media Wiki

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: Where the hosts' verdicts are collected; this one was not essential.

items.name: Bill Elliott's NASCAR Challenge
items.description: The hosts contrast this game with Harlem Globetrotters: Bill Elliott put his name on that game as a designer; the Globetrotters did not. Covered in episode 447.
